messages:
carla-ux: Quick sync — we need a concise precedence rule for gateway match syntax to show in the console and use in routing logic. Host vs path vs service patterns is tripping people in the docs.

carla-ux: Examples we saw: host wildcard + specific path vs specific host + capture path; console currently shows the rule that 'wins' but no explanation.

dave-matcher: TL;DR proposal: score each matcher by specificity. Tie-breaker order idea: 1) static host > wildcard host (fewer wildcards) 2) path specificity (more literal segments, fewer captures/wildcards) 3) explicit service binding wins over inferred service. Final tiebreaker: deterministic creation timestamp.

ben.dev: Concrete example: host *.example.com vs host api.example.com AND paths /users/:id vs /users/me. For request to api.example.com/users/me, the static host and literal path should win -> api.example.com + /users/me route. That matches intuition.

alice: We also need to consider header-derived overrides (eg x-tenant-route) that our console allows. Do we treat header anchors as higher or lower than service binding? UX wants headers surfaced as overrides.

emily: Suggest modeling anchors as orthogonal modifiers that add/subtract from the score. Proposed weights (initial): static-host +100, host-wildcard -10 per wildcard, literal-path-segment +5, capture-segment -2, service-binding +20, header-anchor +30 when present in request. Pseudocode: 

```
score = 0
score += host_static ? 100 : (-10 * host_wildcards)
score += literal_segments * 5
score += capture_segments * -2
score += service_bound ? 20 : 0
score += header_anchor_present ? 30 : 0
```

This makes header anchors impactful but request-scoped.

dave-matcher: That looks reasonable. Two notes: 1) negative wildcard adjustments intentionally drop a wildcard host below literal hosts. 2) header anchors being request-scoped means route winners can flip per request — that's ok but we must explain it in the console.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: matcher-service updated matcher-score v2 -> staging (deploy 3308883000) :white_check_mark:

ben.dev: Catch: header anchors flipping winners is powerful but surprising. Console must show the "why" for a selected request and a canonical "no-anchor" winner in the route list.

carla-ux: UX plan: default console route list shows canonical winner ignoring request-scoped anchors. Add a "request preview" toggle where you can input headers/host/path and see the per-request winner + breakdown (dominant factors badges). Also include example requests showing when winner flips.

jordan: Telemetry: emit matcher.resolve events with shape: matcher.resolve { route_id, reason_scores: ["host:100","path:15","header:30"], request_preview:true }. This will let us measure flip rates during rollout.

alice: Rollout/process note: changing scoring affects live traffic. We must run the scoring v2 against historical logs to compute % of requests that change route, then do a FF canary (5% -> 50% -> 100%) and monitor errors + routing-flip metric. Add an eval harness for this.

dave-matcher: Agreed. I'll draft an RFC with the scoring table, simulation results, and canary plan. Will include a migration script that tags old routes with legacy-score metadata for rollback.

carla-ux: Thanks — I'll mock the console panels to show "dominant factor" badges and the request-preview UI. We'll keep the language terse: "Winner (canonical)" vs "Winner (with headers)".

ben.dev: One more micro-case: service-binding vs header-anchor when both exist and tie — make header-anchor win because it's customer-provided context. Add that to RFC.

dave-matcher: Noted. I'll set header-anchor > service-binding in the weights.

carla-ux: Great work. I'll post the mockups and link RFC when it's up.

carla-ux: (closing) moving this to the matcher RFC thread — thanks all!
